# Accounts Payable Demo App

A multi-entity accounts payable workflow demo that lets AP teams create, approve, track, and import invoices with role-based permissions and entity-aware filtering.

## Features

- Multi-entity support with an entity switcher in the header; every invoice is tied to one entity and lists automatically filter to the selected entity.
- Role-based access for AP Clerk, AP Manager, and Controller, with permissions enforced in the UI and reflected in a role badge in the header.
- End-to-end invoice approval flow: Draft -> Pending Approval -> Approved -> Paid, plus Rejected with a required rejection reason.
- Approval queue for Managers and Controllers, including approve/reject actions and an approval history trail on each invoice.
- Statement Import page for pasting or uploading bank/statement data to detect recurring transactions and highlight patterns for review.

## Demo login

Use the following hardcoded demo credentials to sign in:

- Email: demo@example.com
- Password: demo

The preview app runs with an in-browser fake backend powered by localStorage, so it works immediately without any server setup. When deploying the real application, the frontend swaps to the FastAPI backend implemented in backend/server.py.

## Tech stack

- Vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
- FastAPI
- SQLite

## Quick start

1. Open the app by loading index.html directly in your browser.
2. Optionally start the API backend for persistence and real server-side behavior:

   curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/seed
   curl -X GET http://localhost:8000/health

3. If you are using a local static server, open index.html in the browser and sign in with the demo credentials above.

## Architecture overview

This project is organized as a lightweight single-page frontend with a swappable backend boundary:

- Frontend: plain HTML/CSS/JS renders the login screen, entity switcher, role badge, invoice lists, approval queue, invoice detail view, and statement import workflow.
- Client state: the preview experience stores data in localStorage and uses a fake backend implementation to simulate authentication, invoices, approvals, vendors, and entity filtering.
- Role and entity enforcement: the UI filters all data by selected entity and disables or hides actions based on the current role and invoice state.
- Approval workflow: invoices move through Draft, Pending Approval, Approved, Paid, and Rejected states with a visible audit trail of approval events and rejection reasons.
- Backend: backend/server.py provides the FastAPI service and SQLite persistence used when the demo is deployed or connected to a real API.
- Data model: invoices reference exactly one entity, and the approval logic supports AP Clerk submission plus Manager/Controller approval limits, including unlimited approval for Controllers.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entities (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    code TEXT NOT NULL,
    country TEXT NOT NULL,
    currency TEXT NOT NULL,
    tax_id TEXT,
    is_active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    UNIQUE (user_id, code)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_entities_user_id ON entities(user_id);

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)


def test_health_endpoint():
    response = client.get("/api/health")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    assert "status" in data
    assert data["status"] in {"ok", "healthy", "success"}


def test_login_with_demo_credentials_returns_token():
    payload = {"email": "demo@acme.com", "password": "demo123"}
    response = client.post("/api/auth/login", json=payload)
    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    assert "token" in data or "access_token" in data


def test_login_with_wrong_credentials_returns_401():
    payload = {"email": "demo@acme.com", "password": "wrong-password"}
    response = client.post("/api/auth/login", json=payload)
    assert response.status_code == 401


def test_get_entities_returns_list():
    response = client.get("/api/entities")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    data = response.json()
    assert isinstance(data, list)


def test_create_entity_and_get_shows_new_item():
    create_payload = {"name": "Acme Test Entity"}
    create_response = client.post("/api/entities", json=create_payload)
    assert create_response.status_code == 200
    created = create_response.json()
    assert isinstance(created, dict)
    assert created.get("name") == "Acme Test Entity" or created.get("entity_name") == "Acme Test Entity"

    list_response = client.get("/api/entities")
    assert list_response.status_code == 200
    entities = list_response.json()
    assert any(
        item.get("name") == "Acme Test Entity" or item.get("entity_name") == "Acme Test Entity"
        for item in entities
    )


def test_delete_entity_removes_item():
    create_payload = {"name": "Acme Delete Entity"}
    create_response = client.post("/api/entities", json=create_payload)
    assert create_response.status_code == 200
    created = create_response.json()
    entity_id = created.get("id") or created.get("entity_id")
    assert entity_id is not None

    delete_response = client.delete(f"/api/entities/{entity_id}")
    assert delete_response.status_code in {200, 204}

    list_response = client.get("/api/entities")
    assert list_response.status_code == 200
    entities = list_response.json()
    assert not any(
        item.get("id") == entity_id or item.get("entity_id") == entity_id
        for item in entities
    )
